title.narrative: Skill Up! Building Economic Muscle through Relevant skills to vulnerable Peri/Urban Youth in Kenya

description.narrative: Objective:Young vulnerable people use acquired (labour) market relevant competencies and the provided access to necessary resources & labour market linkages to secure (self-) employment opportunities.Overall objective (Impact):The economic stability and decent income generation of vulnerable young people have improved through gainful / profitable employment or self-employment, resulting in increased food and nutrition security.

Skill development is a mitigation factor to unemployment. The project is envisaged to provide an inclusive learning environment for training opportunities and provision of employment to all, leaving no youth behind.400 Disadvantaged youth will access skills, entrepreneurship, & life skill training. Learners will be linked to prospective employers through internship prior to joining the market. Particular attention is to young teenage mothers and PLWD who are more disadvantaged in seeking for trainings & employment.Training instructors will enhance their skills to bolster their teaching abilities and stay abreast with the evolving market. Significant efforts will be made to provide the youth of opportunities for success through high-quality training relevant to labor market demands.

The proposed intervention seeks enrol learners, 60% of these trainees being women and persons with disability (young teenage mothers / girls at risk and persons with disability). The project will be geared toward increased enrolment for women in courses predominantly dominated by men. Young teenage mothers are given an opportunity to access training, while their young ones are fended for at the day care baby care unit.Latia institute will advertise for a call to scholarship, with special emphasis on young women and persons with disability to apply, shortlist and interview then vet the applicants. A background check of applicants will be conducted to ensure credibility. They will target youth aged between 15 - 35 years old, from poor backgrounds and form four graduates. They will also ensure there is enough accommodation for the apprentices, lessons plan for the classroom training, land preparation and training materials. They will have a team that will be responsible for the implementation and reporting of the project progress.Trainees with receive practical training and lifeskills training at 70/30 ratio respectively.400 Disadvantaged youth aged 15-35 years will access vocational training, entrepreneurship, and life skill training. They will train for 9 months, in WWL and in 2 cohorts at 6 -month interval for the case of LRC.
